captions.instagram:
What is torque?

Torque is what turns things: a push times its distance from the pivot. Undo a stuck wheel nut, balance a seesaw, tip a double-decker bus, test an engine on a brake, crack a walnut, and watch a gyroscope refuse to fall.

→ Torque is force times distance: push harder, or further from the nut, and it turns.
→ The same push near a door’s hinge barely moves it. At the handle, it swings.
→ A seesaw balances when the moments match: 40 kg at 1.5 m equals 30 kg at 2 m.
→ Tilt a full double-decker past about 29° and its centre of gravity leaves the wheels: over it goes.
→ Push down on a 17 cm crank and you make torque. A bigger rear cog multiplies it at the wheel.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/torqueclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is torque? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Torque is what turns things: a push times its distance from the pivot. Undo a stuck wheel nut, balance a seesaw, tip a double-decker bus, test an engine on a brake, crack a walnut, and watch a gyroscope refuse to fall.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/torqueclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/torqueclear

In this video:
• Force times distance. Torque is the turning effect of a force: τ = F × r, in newton-metres.
• Balance. An object stays still when the clockwise and anticlockwise moments match: m₁d₁ = m₂d₂ on a seesaw.
• Machines that turn. A 17 cm bicycle crank turns your push into torque, and the gears change it at the wheel.
• Torque in your hands. When a job needs a set torque, a bigger radius means less force: steering wheels, fat screwdriver handles, nutcrackers and a pipe on a wheel brace.
• Spin, wobble and myths. Unbalanced torque spins things up, τ = Iα.
